summary: U.S. equity markets face renewed pressure on July 19 as semiconductor stocks extended their brutal selloff into a bear market, with the chip sector down 20% from recent highs following a downgrade of SK Hynix by a South Korean brokerage citing risks over fixed-price high-bandwidth memory contracts. Major chipmakers AMD and Nvidia both dropped around 4% on Monday, dragging the broader tech sector lower. The S&P 500 posted its first weekly loss in nearly three months, falling 1.6% last week, while the Nasdaq shed 2.9%. Adding to market jitters, heightened Middle East tensions as the U.S. continues military strikes against Iran have boosted oil prices and fueled broader risk aversion. Investors are also grappling with concerns about AI spending justification, as Chinese startup Moonshot's new Kimi K3 AI model sparked fears of intensifying competition for U.S. tech giants. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve holds rates steady at 3.5%-3.75% as new Chair Kevin Warsh emphasizes commitment to restoring price stability before any easing, with the next FOMC meeting scheduled for July 28-29. Crypto markets showed modest resilience, with Bitcoin trading near $64,600 and Ethereum around $1,870 after earlier gains on softer CPI data were partially reversed by geopolitical tensions.

signals.title: Chip sector enters bear market on SK Hynix downgrade and China AI competition
signals.desc: Semiconductor stocks fell 20% from highs as SK Hynix downgrade over HBM contract risks and China's Kimi K3 AI model launch triggered sector-wide selling pressure across AMD, Nvidia, and chip equipment makers.

signals.title: Fed Chair Warsh holds rates at 3.5%-3.75%, emphasizes price stability focus
signals.desc: The Federal Reserve maintained its hawkish stance in June with no rate cuts signaled and nine of 18 officials penciling in at least one hike this year, dampening hopes for near-term easing.

signals.title: U.S.-Iran conflict escalates, Strait of Hormuz disruption spikes oil prices
signals.desc: Six consecutive days of U.S. airstrikes against Iran have effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, sending oil prices sharply higher and fueling broad risk-off sentiment across equities and crypto.

signals.title: Meta in talks for $10 billion computing deal with Anthropic
signals.desc: Meta is reportedly negotiating a cloud computing rental agreement with AI giant Anthropic worth up to $10 billion, signaling potential shift toward monetizing AI infrastructure amid AI spending scrutiny.

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum hold gains above $64K and $1,850 after CPI relief
signals.desc: Crypto markets stabilized near recent highs with Bitcoin at $64,600 and Ethereum at $1,870 after softer June CPI data bolstered rate-cut hopes, though geopolitical tensions capped further upside.

verdict: Tech weakness and geopolitical risk dominate as chip bear market deepens and Iran tensions flare, though crypto shows surprising resilience amid Fed's hawkish hold.
